On the explicitly authorized blue and red surfaces only, favour a modest reduction of grey admixture so their existing hue families read more distinctly. Keep the original illumination, local light-and-shadow modelling and material character; do not achieve this by increasing exposure, bleaching highlights or darkening the scene. Red accents must remain recognizably red, rather than pink, salmon, beige or neon. Preserve all protected colours and the existing geometry. This is a qualitative local preference, not a global saturation filter.

limitations: Single simplified still-life scene and one palette (cool blue + red); no second scene, no second palette, no person scene.
Three independent random draws per condition; no seed guarantee, so this only compares random spread with the wording effect and cannot give statistical significance.

Sameness and lighting are declared in the content text but the viewer still sees three independently composed illustrations; outline-only differences are reported separately from substantive confounds.

Only the clear direction is tested. Bright/deep, muted, area hierarchy, auxiliary-layer hierarchy, mood/season, material/perception, drawing-style transfer, GPT-image channel, reference images and repaint colour retention are all out of scope.
Deep feature metrics (Gram/AdaIN/LPIPS/CSD) describe whole-image change and cannot be attributed to local de-greying.
No production gate, no threshold and no promise of a stable universal effect.

All three conditions are the same declared direction (clear). Accent surfaces must remain recognizably red; muted is not tested in this round.
